title: An embedded triangular presentation with fraction representations
statement: Let $k$ and $K$ be fields [def-weil-field] with a $k$-algebra structure [def-pc-field-extension], suppose $K=k(b_0,\ldots,b_{m-1})$ for a finite family, and let $x:\operatorname{Fin}(d)\to K$ be a transcendence basis [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis]. There exist $r\geq0$, a nonzero $h\in k[X_0,\ldots,X_{d-1}]$, and monic polynomials $p_i\in k[X_0,\ldots,X_{d+i}][Z]$ ($0\leq i<r$; monic means leading coefficient one) such that, for the explicit list $f$ of [def-weil-pbc-triangular-field-model-equations], the quotient $A=k[X_0,\ldots,X_{d+r}]/(f)$ admits an injective $k$-algebra map $\iota:A\to K$ and every $z\in K$ equals $\iota(a)\iota(s)^{-1}$ for some $a,s\in A$ with $s\ne0$. No regularity claim is made.

proof.text: *The base field $F$ and the tower.* Since $x_1,\dots,x_d$ is a transcendence basis [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis], the $k$-algebra map $k[X_1,\dots,X_d]\to K$, $X_j\mapsto x_j$, is injective, so its image $k[x]=k[x_1,\dots,x_d]$ is a domain isomorphic to the polynomial ring, and $K$ is algebraic over $F:=k(x_1,\dots,x_d)$. The set $\{a/s: a,s\in k[x],\ s\ne0\}$ is a subfield of $K$ containing $k$ and the $x_j$ and is contained in every such subfield, so it is $F$. Put $r:=m$, $L_0:=F$ and $L_i:=F(b_1,\dots,b_i)$ (the smallest subfield of $K$ containing $F$ and $b_1,\dots,b_i$), so $L_i=L_{i-1}(b_i)$; $L_r$ contains $k$ and all $b_j$, hence $L_r\supseteq k(b_1,\dots,b_m)=K$, so $L_r=K$. Each $b_i$ is algebraic over $F$ [def-weil-algebraic-element], hence over $L_{i-1}\supseteq F$ (the same nonzero polynomial).

proof.text: Each generator has a monic minimal polynomial of positive degree over the preceding field. Use the minimal-polynomial quotient isomorphism and its power basis, then Basis.smulTower, to obtain an F-basis of K consisting of bounded monomials in the generators. No separability hypothesis is needed.

proof.text: *The polynomials $P_i$ over $F$.* Fix $i$ and write $\mu_i=T^{e_i}+\sum_{l<e_i}c_{il}T^l$ with $c_{il}\in L_{i-1}$. By step 2 each $c_{il}$ is an $F$-linear combination of monomials in $b_1,\dots,b_{i-1}$; replacing $b_j$ by the variable $Y_j$ gives $g_{il}\in F[Y_1,\dots,Y_{i-1}]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] with $g_{il}(b_1,\dots,b_{i-1})=c_{il}$. Put $P_i:=Y_i^{e_i}+\sum_{l<e_i}g_{il}Y_i^l\in F[Y_1,\dots,Y_i]$. Then $P_i$ is monic of degree $e_i$ in $Y_i$ with coefficients in $F[Y_1,\dots,Y_{i-1}]$, and $P_i(b_1,\dots,b_i)=\mu_i(b_i)=0$ in $K$.

proof.text: Lift each coefficient a/h^j to a(X) T^j, preserving the leading coefficient one. Assemble the resulting equations using [def-weil-pbc-triangular-field-model-equations]. The localization presentation identifies quotienting by hT - 1 with adjoining 1/h. Taking the further quotient by the lifted monic equations identifies the explicit polynomial quotient A with B = D[Y]/(P).

Source also read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07BV and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08JZ because the local literature checkout is absent.

proof.text: *$B_i$ is free over $D$.* For $0\le i\le r$ put $B_i:=D[Y_1,\dots,Y_i]/(P_1,\dots,P_i)$ and $E_i:=\prod_{j\le i}\{0,\dots,e_j-1\}$. Claim: the classes of $Y^\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon\in E_i$, form a basis of $B_i$ as a $D$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. For $i=0$, $B_0=D$ with basis $\{1\}$. For $i\ge1$: $P_1,\dots,P_{i-1}$ do not involve $Y_i$, so taking the quotient in two stages $B_i\cong B_{i-1}[Y_i]/(\bar P_i)$, $\bar P_i$ the image of $P_i$, which is monic of degree $e_i$ in $Y_i$ (step 4). By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], $1,Y_i,\dots,Y_i^{e_i-1}$ is a $B_{i-1}$-basis of $B_i$, and by the induction hypothesis and [lem-weil-pbc-tower-product-basis] (for $D\to B_{i-1}$ and the $B_{i-1}$-module $B_i$) the products $Y^\varepsilon Y_i^l$, i.e. the $Y^{\varepsilon'}$, $\varepsilon'\in E_i$, form a $D$-basis of $B_i$.

Source also read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07BV and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08JZ because the local literature checkout is absent.

proof.text: *The map $\iota_0:B_r\to K$: injective, and $K$ is its field of fractions.* The $D$-algebra map $D[Y_1,\dots,Y_r]\to K$, $Y_j\mapsto b_j$ ($D\subseteq F\subseteq K$), kills every $P_i$ (step 4), so it induces a $k$-algebra map $\iota_0:B_r\to K$ with $\iota_0(Y^\varepsilon)=b^\varepsilon$. If $\iota_0(\sum_{\varepsilon\in E_r}d_\varepsilon Y^\varepsilon)=\sum d_\varepsilon b^\varepsilon=0$ with $d_\varepsilon\in D\subseteq F$, then all $d_\varepsilon=0$ because the $b^\varepsilon$ are $F$-linearly independent (step 2); by step 6 every element of $B_r$ is such a sum, so $\iota_0$ is injective. Every $z\in K$ is $\sum_\varepsilon q_\varepsilon b^\varepsilon$ with $q_\varepsilon\in F$ (step 2); writing $q_\varepsilon=a_\varepsilon/s$ with one common $s\in k[x]\setminus\{0\}$ (the product of the denominators, step 1) gives $z=\iota_0(\sum a_\varepsilon Y^\varepsilon)\,\iota_0(s)^{-1}$, where $\iota_0(s)=s\neq0$ in $K$ and hence $s\neq0$ in $B_r$. Transport the map and fraction representations across the quotient presentation of the previous step. This proves exactly the claimed injection and fraction representations, without asserting regularity.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_triangularFieldModel_presentation
    (k : Type u) (K : Type v) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (hfg : ∃ (m : ℕ) (b : Fin m → K), IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range b) = ⊤)
    (d : ℕ) (x : Fin d → K) (hx : IsTranscendenceBasis k x) :
    ∃ (r : ℕ) (h : MvPolynomial (Fin d) k)
      (p : (i : Fin r) → Polynomial (MvPolynomial (Fin (d + 1 + i.val)) k)),
      h ≠ 0 ∧ (∀ i, (p i).Monic) ∧
      let A := MvPolynomial (Fin (d + 1 + r)) k ⧸
        Ideal.ofList (triangularFieldModelEquations k d r h p)
      ∃ (ι : A →ₐ[k] K), Function.Injective ι ∧
        ∀ z : K, ∃ a s : A, s ≠ 0 ∧ z = ι a * (ι s)⁻¹
